findings.title: The Library's check for an upload URL signed with no R2 account never fires: the real host is <bucket>.undefined.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
findings.scenario: I ran getSignedUploadUrl with R2_ACCOUNT_ID, R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and R2_PUBLIC_URL unset. The upload URL's host was `servd-media.undefined.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`: the S3 client puts the bucket in the host name, and R2_BUCKET_NAME defaults to servd-media. `presignedWithoutAccount()` (line 56) tests the host against /^(undefined|null)?\.?r2\.cloudflarestorage\.com$/i, which fails for that host; I checked this in node. So the guard the builder describes ("catches an upload URL the API signed with no R2 account… shows the message once") never runs. When /health can't be read, or the API has no uploadStorage check yet (state 'unknown', button enabled), each file still goes to a host that can't resolve. Each file then fails on its own with the CORS message ("Usually the storage bucket is not set up to take uploads from this admin site (CORS) — ask IT"), which names the wrong cause.
findings.fix: Match any host that has an `undefined` or `null` label before r2.cloudflarestorage.com, e.g. /(^|\.)(undefined|null)\.r2\.cloudflarestorage\.com$/i. Better still, as the builder's own follow-up suggests: GET /media/upload-url should refuse with 503 STORAGE_NOT_CONFIGURED when the R2 env is missing, and the Library should handle that code.

findings.title: Marketing and brand_manager now get narrow GET /concepts rows inside the full Brand Editor (/marketing/brands), which shows them as blank brands and then fails to save with 403
findings.scenario: marketing and brand_manager hold the 'brands' module (moduleAccess.ts:130/135; workspaces.ts:71 puts 'brands' next to 'storefront'), so /marketing/brands is in their sidebar. That page calls GET /concepts?includeInactive=1. Before this change it got a 403 and the editor was empty. It now gets STOREFRONT_CONCEPT_SELECT rows, and BrandForm (marketing/brands/page.tsx:222-262) fills its form from them. Description, the whole brief, contact details, heroTagline, storefrontVisible, reservationsEnabled, STRN/NTN, province and invoice fields all show empty. The tax rates show the 15/8 placeholders, not the brand's real rates. The list subtitle reads 'slug · undefined', since `type` is not in the narrow select. A marketer sees what looks like a wiped brand. Save sends a full PATCH that gets 403 (MANAGERS only), so no data is lost today. If PATCH is ever opened to marketing, as the page title 'the one brand editor' in the marketing workspace suggests, Save would null every field the narrow row lacks.
findings.fix: Keep the narrow rows away from the brand editor. Options: give BrandForm a read-only or 'not allowed' state when the row has no full fields or the role can't PATCH, or have /marketing/brands run its query only for roles that pass the PATCH gate (MANAGERS). Alternatively, give the Storefront editor its own scoped list (e.g. GET /site-layouts/brands) instead of widening GET /concepts, which every admin page shares.

findings.title: The CEO can no longer approve an unsubmitted draft from the editor, although the API supports it on purpose
findings.scenario: Approve now shows only when draftStatus is 'pending' or 'scheduled' (`isAdmin && submitted`, line ~293). The API's approve accepts a plain 'draft' by design: siteLayouts/routes.ts:442 refuses only 'none', and lines 451-452 record `submittedById ?? draftUpdatedById` "to keep a submitter on record". The CEO used to edit a page and press Approve, which saved and published in one step. He now has to press Submit (which notifies himself) and then Approve. A draft marketing saved but never submitted, or a rejected draft, can't be published from the editor until someone submits it. The fix for the untouched-page 404 only needed hasSavedDraft; the old Approve gate `(!hasDraft && !dirty)` plus ensureSaved would already have saved first.
findings.fix: Show Approve to admin whenever there is a saved draft or local edits, as before. Keep ensureSaved() before approve for the CEO's own edits, now that hasDraft uses hasSavedDraft() and an untouched page saves first. To keep the guarantee that he approves exactly what was submitted, disable Approve only when the row is 'pending' and was submitted by someone else, and there are unsaved local edits.
